genZNote: One half of the yogurt duo — it warms things up (literally, thermophilic) while Lactobacillus bulgaricus brings the tang.

habitat.hostAssociation: Not part of normal human microbiota; used as a food-grade starter culture
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Industrially propagated for yogurt and some cheese production

identificationClues: Thrives at higher temperatures (~40-45°C) than most streptococci, hence 'thermophilus'
Catalase-negative, chain-forming coccus like other streptococci
Works symbiotically with Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus in traditional yogurt fermentation
Non-hemolytic and considered food-safe (GRAS status) — an important contrast to the pyogenic streptococci

examFacts.importantDisease: None — food-grade organism, not a pathogen
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Thermophilic dairy starter culture, paired with L. bulgaricus to make yogurt
